extra_quotes: Training data were generated by forward calculations based on the Fresnel equations, following our previous DLE study.6
In the case of Unified-FiLM, a total of 165 million samples obtained by combining Datasets 1–3 were used.
Training was performed with the Adam optimizer on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU (24 GB) and required 72 h 14 min for Unified-FiLM.

Experimental validation on 47 thin-film samples across diverse substrates yielded sample-averaged mean absolute errors, relative to conventional manual analysis, of 0.047 for refractive index, 0.030 for extinction coefficient, and 1.52 nm for thickness, with each analysis completed in under 2 s.

In contrast, as highlighted by the orange background in Fig. 3, when the thicknesses of overlayers on substrates are large (≥ 100 nm) or a substrate has a complex multilayer structure, the prediction accuracy degrades rather notably.
